title: Decode loop execution
statement: Fix a finite nondeterministic Turing machine $N$, a mode, a bit string $y$, a bound $B$, a decode identifier $c$, a bit string $w$, and a register assignment $v$ to the 21 registers. Suppose every suffix value of $w$ is at most $B$; every register value under $v$ is at most $B$; the pointer register equals the base register plus the stride for $c$ times $|w|$; the accumulator and temporary registers are zero; and, at each position $i<|w|$, the input bit at the base offset by the stride times $i$ equals the $i$th bit of $w$. Then the codec program in the given mode, starting at its decode-test instruction with assignment $v$, reaches its next instruction for $c$ with the pointer reset to its base value and the accumulator equal to the binary value of $w$, leaving all other registers unchanged. Every configuration before the endpoint satisfies the program's safety condition and has all register values at most $B$.
